text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming.p99 latency breach detected in us-west-1. p99=7.2s (SLO=2.5s) sustained for 6m, error rate for streaming routes up x3. Link: https://dash.redwood.example/streams?range=6m

sarah: paging oncall — @leo are you on shift?

leo: oncall here, looking. can folks drop any quick diffs? is this an infra or model perf issue?

mike: grabbing telemetry now. tail traces show a cluster of stalls in step "kv_fetch" and long GPU kernels on encoder. infra counters: ECC correctable spikes on node gpu-wn-42, +1.2k correctables over 5m. thermal warnings reported 3x in last 10m.

mike: paste logs:
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,enc_util --format=csv
0, A100-80GB, 98%, 83C, 96%
... node gpu-wn-42
```
```
[  143.124123] NVRM: Ecc: Correctable error, type: 0x01
[  143.124456] nv_peer_mem: detected ECC correction
[  145.512321] gpu temp critical threshold reached
```

anya: ok immediate mitigation: isolate gpu-wn-42 and reroute streaming traffic away while we investigate. I'll kick a route update and start node drain.

kyle: +1 to reroute. also propose enabling the fallback model variant (quantized small) for streaming routes to cut per-token GPU work until healthy capacity is restored. reduces quality slightly but avoids timeouts.

leo: do it. anya, post the exact commands here so we have an audit trail.

anya: running: 
```
# cordon + drain
redwoodctl node cordon --node=gpu-wn-42 --reason="elec/thermal-ecc-spike"
redwoodctl node drain --node=gpu-wn-42 --grace-period=30s
# update routing to avoid node
redwoodctl route update --selector region=us-west --exclude-node=gpu-wn-42
# enable fallback model for streaming routes
redwoodctl rollout start --route=streaming.* --model=redwood/stream-small-quant --priority=emergency
```

ops-bot: Action started: cordon gpu-wn-42 (id: act-8891). Drain tasks scheduled.

mike: note: draining will cause inflight streams to reconnect -> transient increase in p50 but should improve tail. also observed KV cache miss rate jumped 40% in affected pods, likely due to the eviction of some long-lived pods.

lisa: CS standby — I'm drafting a customer note for impacted tenants in us-west. sending SL docs to legal for approval. sample: "We're seeing elevated streaming latency in us-west, some streams may experience stalls; mitigations are in progress."

customer-success-bot: Template sent to CS channel for review.

leo: infra, can we provision a replacement GPU node in the coloc? if this is thermal/hardware we should swap hardware rather than keep recycling.

mike: requested hw swap with colo team (ticket #COL-3321). also running a soft-reset on GPU driver stack on the node to confirm whether it's flaky or persistent.

ops-bot: Drain progress: 15/20 pods evicted from gpu-wn-42. ETA ~2m.

mike: after cordon/drain, initial improvement: p99 dropped from 7.2s -> 3.6s. still above SLO but trending better. some streaming stalls persist tied to KV backpressure on fallback hosts.

kyle: rolling back model isn't ideal long-term. short-term fallback stays. Also enable extra worker replicas for streaming-quant nodes: 
```
redwoodctl scale --route=streaming.* --replicas=+30% --timeout=120s
```

anya: route update applied, fallback rollout in progress (50% traffic shifted). watch: https://dash.redwood.example/streams/rollouts/act-8892

sarah: customer impact: observed timeouts and partial stream truncation for ~12 tenants on dedicated/dedicated-plus in us-west between 12:18-12:44 UTC. CS notified. No billing adjustments yet; we'll assess after stabilized.

leo: assigning owner for incident review: sara-h (infra lead) + mike (runtime). please collect kernel logs, thermal sensor history, NVME power draw, and GPU ECC hist over last 24h.

mike: copying logs to incident bucket s3://incidents/1768132468/; also running a diagnostic script that will collect ECC counters every 30s.

ops-bot: Replacement node request COL-3321 acknowledged by colo team, ETA 45m for on-site swap.

mike: further notes from dmesg: occasional PCIe link resets observed, could be indicative of hardware degradation.

kyle: if PCIe flakiness is causing stalls, we should consider routing streaming heavy RPCs to other racks until swap. Can we do rack-level exclusion?

anya: yes, applied rack-level avoid policy for streaming: redwoodctl route update --exclude-rack=rack-07-west

leo: status update to exec/ops: short summary: p99 outage induced by hardware-level ECC/thermal degradation on gpu-wn-42 causing streaming stalls -> mitigations: cordon+drain node, reroute traffic, enable quantized fallback, scale replicas. p99 improved from 7.2s -> 3.6s and trending down. colo swap in progress.

sarah: thanks team. next steps: 1) validate replacement node and rejoin healthy pool, 2) run extended stress test to catch thermal hysteresis, 3) post-incident writeup with action items (diagnostics, monitor thresholds, auto-evacuate rule).

customer-success-bot: Customer message sent to affected tenants at 12:38 UTC: "We're investigating elevated streaming latency in us-west; we've routed traffic to healthy capacity and applied temporary fallbacks. We'll follow up with a full incident report."

mike: quick mitigation follow-up: after rack exclusion + extra replicas + fallback, p99 now at 2.1s within SLO for the last 3m. keeping monitoring windows open for 30m.

leo: closing page for now but keeping incident open for postmortem. assigning postmortem owner: mike. Expected postmortem draft ETA: EOD.

sarah: :white_check_mark: thanks everyone. add retro item: consider auto-trigger for node cordon when ECC correctable rate crosses 500/min to avoid manual pages.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: SEV-2 -> will transition to follow-up. Logs and timeline archived at s3://incidents/1768132468/timeline.json

sarah: locking this thread; follow-ups will be in #postmortems.
